target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): do not wipe archive on user-typed [cron: prefix
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`memory_search` silently drops all indexed content from a reset/deleted session archive when **any** user message in the transcript starts with `[cron:`. The user's prompt is treated as a server-set cron-run signal, which wipes everything collected so far and skips every remaining message — so unrelated remembered facts (vendor, budget, etc.) become unsearchable in the archive even though the live transcript stays intact. Reproducer and root-cause analysis: #98241.

This contradicts both the contract comment in `session-files.ts:111-113` (usage-counted archives "must stay indexed so `memory_search` can surface hits on post-reset / post-delete history") and the safety comment a few lines below the buggy block, which already warns that user-typed text can match these patterns and that a cross-message drop must not happen.

## Why This Change Was Made

The text-based cross-message wipe in `buildSessionEntry` (the `!generatedByCronRun && allowArchiveContentCronClassification && isGeneratedCronPromptMessage(...)` branch) was unsafe: `DIRECT_CRON_PROMPT_RE = /^\[cron:[^\]]+\]\s*/` matches ordinary human text. A user pasting a cron log line, or asking "[cron:daily-digest] why did my digest job fail last night?", is enough to flip the whole archive to cron-generated and wipe all earlier + later content.

The structured `isCronRunGeneratedRecord` check earlier in the same function reads `sessionKey` provenance set by the gateway — user text cannot spoof that. The per-message cron-prompt drop still happens correctly inside `sanitizeSessionText` (so the actual cron-prefixed user prompt itself stays omitted), but it no longer cascades into a full-archive wipe.

## User Impact

- Reset or deleted session archives containing a user message that starts with `[cron:` will now stay searchable in `memory_search` for everything except the cron-prefixed prompt itself (which is still dropped per-message by `sanitizeSessionText`).
- No behavior change for archives without such a user message, and no change to the live `.jsonl` indexing.
- No new config or migration surface; no compatibility shim — buggy branch is removed.

## Evidence

Reproducer mirrors the issue's transcript exactly (4 messages: user `[cron:daily-digest] ...`, assistant reply, user remember request, assistant confirm). Added a regression test in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts`:

- `generatedByCronRun` is falsy
- indexed content contains the assistant reply and the unrelated "Please remember: my preferred vendor is Acme Robotics" exchange
- `lineMap` is `[2, 3, 4]` (the dropped `[cron:` user prompt becomes line 1, the rest are indexed)

Removed the prior test `keeps cron-run deleted archives opaque when the live session store entry is gone` because it enshrined the buggy behavior (asserting `content === ""` and `lineMap === []` for an archive triggered by user text). The structured-provenance path is still covered by the next test `keeps cron-run reset archives opaque when session metadata preserves the cron key`.

Local typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` → exit 0. Local oxlint on touched files: clean.

Fixes #98241
